newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq says spreads decline after pricing change.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq says spreads decline after pricing change.

text.p: The Nasdaq Stock Market said Thursday an analysis showed that bid and ask spreads on average declined six percent Monday and Tuesday after a change to quoting stock prices in increments of 1/16 of a dollar.

The National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotation system said it analyzed the spread between the bid and ask on the first 450 stocks that were phased in under new Securities and Exchange Commission Order Handling Rules.
The new system on Nasdaq started June 2. Before the change, the smallest increment was 1/8.

"Early results show that, as expected, quoting in smaller increments can enhance transparency and price discovery," Frank Zarb, chairman, chief executive and president of the Nasdaq parent company, the National Association of Securities Dealers Inc, said in a statement. "This is preliminary data, and we will continue to monitor the results of the move."

A Nasdaq spokesman said Nasdaq stocks have been trading in increments of 16ths, 32nds, and 64ths for some time, but not quoted in those increments. Now they have gone down to the 16ths in quoting the issues, as well.
